title: A New Covenant, a New Heart
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Israel's history shows the old system failing again and again, and so does my own heart. The new covenant is fulfilled in Jesus, who gives us new hearts.
exhortation: Israel needed this promise so badly. They needed something new, because what they were doing wasn't working. You can't read the history of the Old Testament and conclude that the system was working: that the laws, ceremonies, sacrifices and punishments were achieving the salvation of Israel. They weren't. Over and over, Israel's history was one of failure. They despised the Lord's teaching and turned away. They couldn't do it.

But when I read this, I don't look down on Israel. I look at my own heart and see the same rebellion, the same quickness to turn from the Lord. I need this prophecy. I need this new heart. If I don't have the law written on my heart and the Spirit of God in me, I'm just as doomed.

This promise came in the middle of terrible judgment. For seventy years Israel wept by the rivers of Babylon. A remnant did return. They laid the stones of the temple, raised the gates of Jerusalem and rebuilt the walls of their fathers. But ultimately they were rebuilding the same system that had failed. The real fulfillment of this prophecy isn't in the temple or the walls of Jerusalem. It is in the final conquering of sin and the softening of the human heart, accomplished in the work of Jesus Christ.

Now we live in the days when this prophecy is truly fulfilled. We don't need priests, temples or prophets to tell us what to do. Jesus is our forever priest, every Christian is a temple, and the word of God is all we need for life and godliness, with his Spirit poured out not on a select few but on everyone who trusts in the name of the Lord. What can we do but respond in worship? Consider the mercy of God, who looked on sinners and rebels who hated him and killed his prophets, and looked on us with compassion. He took the first step to restore a people to himself and put a new heart in them that would worship in spirit and truth.
prayer: God, thank you that we can put our full faith and trust in the work you have done, and that you are still working and will complete what you started. It's so easy to doubt that when we stumble into sin, or when suffering gets hard. We can turn away from you in fear and begin to doubt.

But there is no doubt in you. You have always been faithful, and you proved it definitively at the cross, where you shed your blood for us while we were your enemies and at our worst. We're so grateful that we can put our full trust in you. Help us do that today as we go about our day. In Jesus' name, amen.
